Newton printed the hymn under Luke 13:6–9. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

6Then Jesus told this parable: “A man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard. He went to look for fruit on it, but did not find any. 7So he said to the keeper of the vineyard, ‘Look, for the past three years I have come to search for fruit on this fig tree and haven’t found any. Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?’ 8‘Sir,’ the man replied, ‘leave it alone again this year, until I dig around it and fertilize it. 9If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, you can cut it down.’” LUKE 13:6–9 · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ LUKE 13
The under gard’ner grieves, In vain his strength he spends, For heaps of useless leaves, Afford him small amends: He hears the LORD his will make known, To cut the barren fig–trees down. STANZA III
